summary: L-4 cab built on Johnson Mountain in 1938, abandoned 1959, now gone; sources give no staffing or fire record and one undated photo hints at footings.

facts.status_note: Cab listed as gone by the Former Fire Lookout Sites and firelookout.com; an undated WillhiteWeb.com photo caption suggests footings may remain.

access.note: Reached on foot by a long hike inside the Glacier Peak Wilderness; no source gives a formal access rule for the site.

visit.trail_note: About 9.5 miles one way from the North Fork Sauk River trailhead, gaining roughly 5,700 feet. WillhiteWeb.com describes following Pilot Ridge Trail to its southwest ridge, then a half-mile climb up the former lookout trail.

events.note: An L-4 cab was constructed on the site.
Abandoned, as all three sources state.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register as US 1964, WA 463, on April 3, 2020.

notes_for_editor: Brief record is consistent with all three sources: built 1938, abandoned 1959, FFLOS US 1964, WA 463 registered April 3, 2020, elevation 2048.6 m matches 2,049 m. Brief coordinates (47.99476, -121.171624) match the FFLOS page; a firelookout.org listing gives 47.99499, -121.17257, about 75 m away. No source read gives staffing, fire, or builder records, so none are stated. The Weebly Rex's Fire Lookout page lists the site as Removed (corroborates gone; not cited). The access level 'public' is an inference from the wilderness hike route, not a stated rule. The footings photo is undated and rests on one caption. The Wikipedia article on the mountain was not read.
